errors.reasoning: GetUserByIDWithResourceOwner's scanUser returns this when the SQL row scan finds no matching row (or count != 1) for the given userId, i.e. the requested user does not exist.
scanUser returns this for any non-ErrNoRows scan failure while reading the single user row looked up by GetUserByID.

userCheckPermission invokes the injected permissionCheck (domain.PermissionUserRead) whenever the caller is requesting a user other than themselves; getUserPermissions throws this if the request context has no auth/ctx data.
Reached from the same permission check path when the caller has no memberships at all (org or instance-wide) to evaluate for the user.read permission on the target user.
checkUserResourcePermissions throws this when the caller's memberships yield zero permissions matching user.read, denying access to the requested user's data.
Thrown when the caller has some user.read permissions but none that are global or scoped to this specific target userId (resourceID).
removeUserDependencies calls query.UserGrants to look up the target user's grants for cascading removal; this fires if building the SQL statement for that user-grants lookup fails.
removeUserDependencies calls s.query.Memberships to gather the user's org/project/instance memberships to cascade-remove; fires if the SQL statement build for that membership search fails.
getGroupsByUserID calls SearchGroupUsers to find groups the user belongs to (for cascading removal); fires if the group-users search query construction fails.
Same getGroupsByUserID -> SearchGroupUsers call; fires on a DB/query execution error while fetching the user's group memberships.
RemoveUserV2's first check: thrown if the userId on the DeleteUser request is empty.
Thrown when the loaded userRemoveWriteModel shows the user does not exist (already removed or never existed), i.e. deleting a non-existent user.
checkPermissionDeleteUser -> newPermissionCheck calls c.checkPermission (user.delete) on the target user's resource owner; fails with this if the caller's context/auth data is missing.
Same permission-check path for user.delete (and the user.delete.self fallback for self-deletion); thrown if the caller has no memberships to derive permissions from.
Thrown when the caller lacks any permission matching user.delete (or user.delete.self when deleting themselves) needed to remove this user.
Thrown when the caller has user.delete-family permissions but none scoped globally or to this specific target userId.
RemoveUserV2 wraps any error from loading the org's (or instance's) domain policy while deciding org-scoped-username handling for the UserRemovedEvent, surfacing it as a precondition failure.

Underlying cause wrapped by COMMAND-l40ykb3xh2: (c *Commands) domainPolicyWriteModel throws this if neither the organization nor the instance has an existing domain policy, which should not normally happen but is the actual reachable Throw site.
LockUserV2's first check: thrown if the userId on the LockUser request is empty.
Thrown when the loaded user state write model shows the user does not exist (deleted or never existed).
Thrown when the user exists but is in a state other than Active or Initial (e.g. already locked or inactive), since only those states can be locked.
checkPermissionUpdateUser -> newPermissionCheck calls c.checkPermission (user.write) on the target user's resource owner; fails with this if the caller's context/auth data is missing.
Same user.write permission-check path; thrown if the caller has no memberships at all to derive permissions from.
Thrown when the caller lacks any permission matching user.write needed to lock this user.
Thrown when the caller has some user.write permissions but none scoped globally or to this specific target userId.
